title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context and caveats. The page is a fragment written in French over the back of an unrelated English typescript. That typescript, visible through the paper, is the same Kodaira-type vanishing/embedding argument seen on the neighbouring pages (sheaves O_V[nE], H^1 = 0 for n large). The handwriting is very hard to read, so the following is tentative.

Setting. The manuscript belongs to the 1965 notes on the Galois theory of motives. Here Grothendieck works over the real numbers. G_R is a real form of the motivic Galois group: the Tannakian group of motives over R, which includes the action of complex conjugation. He considers 'G_R-variétés de type fini sur R'.

Main sentence, plausible reading. 'Le cône qui exprime cette effectivité est engendré par les rayons définis par les γ(s')' (inserted: 'sous forme semi-algébrique'). In modern terms:
- A motive, i.e. a representation V of the motivic group, is effective when its Hodge weights are nonnegative.
- Those weights are the weights of V restricted along the Hodge cocharacters γ(s'): G_m → G_R. Here s' runs over (real) points parametrising the Hodge structures, or the conjugates of the Hodge cocharacter.
- So 'effective' is a positivity condition with respect to a cone in the cocharacter space, generated by the rays R_+·γ(s'). Equivalently, the effective characters form the dual cone.

Next sentences. He seems to say this amounts to a property of certain subsets 𝒢(s') ⊂ G_R^{γ(s')}(R). Here G_R^{γ(s')} is probably the centraliser of γ(s'), and the subsets are described 'par leurs valeurs propres' (by eigenvalues) in the representations of G_R^{γ(s')}. The claim that these subsets are algebraic (semi-algebraic) varieties is flagged as 'une condition arithmétique assez draconienne!'.

What it serves. Grothendieck is trying to say which reductive groups, equipped with which families of cocharacters, can occur as motivic Galois groups over R. The family of Hodge cocharacters, and the positivity (effectivity) structure they define, must satisfy strong algebraicity and integrality constraints. This is a precursor of the question 'which groups are Mumford–Tate / motivic Galois groups'.
errors: No checkable error: the text is a fragmentary sketch with illegible words. The claimed equivalence (effectivity cone generated by Hodge cocharacter rays) is plausible but stated without proof.
Calling algebraicity of the eigenvalue loci an 'arithmetic' condition is a heuristic remark, not a precise statement.

ideas.what: Effectivity of real motives expressed as a positivity cone generated by rays from Hodge cocharacters γ(s') of the real motivic Galois group G_R
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter / weight cone; effective motives characterised by nonnegative Hodge weights
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, Shimura varieties 1979); Serre, 'Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques' (1994)
ideas.where_published: unsure; only Saavedra Rivano's Catégories tannakiennes (1972) develops Grothendieck's Tannakian framework

ideas.what: Algebraicity (semi-algebraicity) of eigenvalue-defined loci in centralisers G_R^{γ(s')}(R) seen as a strong arithmetic restriction on which groups can be motivic Galois groups
ideas.modern_name: Constraints on Mumford–Tate / motivic Galois groups (which reductive groups with cocharacter data occur)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1994); Green–Griffiths–Kerr, Mumford–Tate groups and domains (2012); Simpson

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a description of the effectivity structure of real motives as a cone generated by rays attached to Hodge cocharacters, presented semi-algebraically. He notes that algebraicity of the associated eigenvalue loci is a draconian arithmetic condition on the motivic group over R. The thread is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: sont des variétés algébriques, ce qui est une condition arithmétique assez draconienne!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early (1965) form of the problem of characterising motivic / Mumford–Tate groups through their Hodge cocharacters and positivity (effectivity) cones. That problem was later treated by Serre and by Green–Griffiths–Kerr. The 'effective cone' viewpoint on the real motivic group is not standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The fragment shows Grothendieck already in 1965 thinking of effectivity of motives as a cone defined by Hodge cocharacters over R, with algebraicity constraints on the motivic group. The ideas are close to known later work (Deligne, Serre), and the page is too illegible and fragmentary to extract a definite unpublished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 'Le cas [?]' is more likely 'Le cône'.
Line 2 'peut exprimer cette effectivité est [-...-] {+surprenante+}' is more likely 'qui exprime cette effectivité est engendré' ('engendré' underlined, possibly overwritten).
Line 3: 'par les rayons définis par les γ(s')', with the insertion 'sous forme "semi-algébrique"' above.
Line 5 'fibrations' is uncertain. The symbol looks like 𝒻(s') or 𝒢(s') ⊂ G_R^{γ(s')}(R), and 'variétés' there may be another word, e.g. 'orbites' or 'ventes' is unclear.
Line 7: 'de G_R^{γ(s')} — est un fait connu des' is uncertain. G_R(R) was written and struck out before the superscript.
Line 8: the underlined word before 'algébriques' may be 'orbites' or 'variétés'.
The background typescript (English, Kodaira-type vanishing argument, as on adjacent pages) is unrelated scrap paper, not part of this note.
